synopsis: UNECE’s New Assessment/Test Method (NATM) was developed by VMAD, an informal group under GRVA [f1281, f15392]. NATM combines five evidence pillars— audit and assessment, virtual testing, track testing, real-world testing and in-service monitoring—rather than treating simulation as standalone evidence [f1282, f15407]. Chapter 6 describes its credibility assessment framework as introduced for virtual testing under UN R152, requiring evidence of accuracy, robustness, documentation, verification and validation, calibration and sensitivity analysis [f4829, f4830]. The glossary additionally identifies toolchain management, analysis and uncertainty, and requires the credibility assessment’s outcome to define the envelope in which a virtual tool may be used [f15408, f15409]. EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 includes an annex related to NATM and states that simulation shall not substitute for physical tests; the supplied facts concern on-road applications and do not establish applicability to heavy off-road machines [f15410, f1282, f4829].
